comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue increased to 49% in 2024 from 46% in 2023. This increase was primarily driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues, as well as lower Gaming revenue, which was partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVDA reported significant gross margin improvements in fiscal 2024 driven by strong Data Center revenue performance. NVDA’s gross margin rose to 72.7% from 56.9%, primarily due to a 217% increase in Data Center revenue and lower net inventory provisions. Similarly, AMD’s gross margin increased to 49% from 46%, driven by a favorable revenue mix shift toward higher Data Center and Client revenues. While both companies benefited from Data Center growth, NVDA’s margin expansion was more substantial (15.8 percentage points vs AMD's 3 percentage points) and specifically highlighted lower inventory provisions, whereas AMD focused on the revenue mix shift.

sentences.text: Our overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023.
The year over year increase was primarily due to strong Data Center revenue growth of 217% and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue was 49% in 2024 compared to 46% in 2023.
The increase in gross margin was due to a favorable shift in revenue mix of higher Data Center and Client revenues, lower Gaming revenue, partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.

comparisons.peer_topic: Gross margin financial results and VMware impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin increased to $32,509 million in fiscal year 2024 from $24,690 million in fiscal year 2023, primarily due to VMware contributions offset by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets. As a percentage of net revenue, gross margin decreased to 63% from 69%, driven by the same amortization factors, less favorable semiconductor product mix, and offsets from infrastructure software margins.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA both disclosed gross margin metrics for fiscal 2024, but the trends and drivers were divergent. NVDA’s overall gross margin increased to 72.7%, driven by Data Center revenue growth. AVGO’s gross margin as a percentage of net revenue actually decreased to 63% from 69%, primarily due to higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger and less favorable semiconductor product mix. While both companies operate in similar infrastructure spaces, AVGO faced structural margin pressures from acquisition amortization, whereas NVDA benefited from organic revenue growth and favorable inventory conditions.

sentences.text: Our overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023.
The year over year increase was primarily due to strong Data Center revenue growth of 217% and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
The decrease was primarily due to higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger.
In addition, gross margin contributions from our infrastructure software segment were partially offset by less favorable margin within the semiconductor solutions segment driven by product mix.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Impairment and Depreciation Charges Impacting Gross Margin
comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation charges related to manufacturing assets exceeding capacity for the Intel 7 process node, as well as $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges.
comparisons.comparison: In stark contrast to NVDA’s margin expansion, INTC reported a decline in consolidated gross margin in 2024. NVDA’s gross margin increased to 72.7%, aided by lower net inventory provisions, whereas INTC’s gross margin decreased by $4.4 billion (or 20%) due to $3.3 billion in impairment and accelerated depreciation charges and $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges. While NVDA saw inventory costs as a tailwind or neutral factor due to lower provisions, INTC faced significant headwinds from inventory write-downs and asset impairments related to manufacturing capacity issues.

sentences.text: Our overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023.
The year over year increase was primarily due to strong Data Center revenue growth of 217% and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
Our consolidated gross margin in 2024 decreased by $4.4 billion, or 20%, compared to 2023 due primarily to higher 2024 impairment charges and accelerated depreciation.

Our 2024 gross margin also decreased due to lower revenue, higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 4 and Intel 7 products, higher period charges due to $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges recognized in 2024, and higher factory start-up costs.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and MU reported improved gross margins in fiscal 2024 following difficult prior-year conditions, though the magnitude and drivers differed. NVDA’s gross margin increased to 72.7% from 56.9%, driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions. MU’s consolidated gross margin improved significantly to 22% from -9% in 2023, aided by higher average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, as well as lower costs from selling inventories written down in the prior year. Both companies saw inventory-related issues in the prior year (NVDA had provisions in 2023, MU had write-downs), but NVDA’s 2024 performance was characterized by revenue growth, while MU’s was characterized by price and cost recovery.
